name: hollow_section
description: Section-Mapped Process Hollowing — an advanced injection technique combining T1055.012 (process hollowing) with T1055 section-mapping delivery. Attacker launches a fresh TestTarget process CREATE_SUSPENDED, creates a shared RWX section, maps it into its own address space (locally writes shellcode), then maps the same section into the suspended victim (fires KERNEL_THREATINT_TASK_MAPVIEW cross-process — no VirtualAllocEx or WriteProcessMemory needed), redirects the victim's main thread RIP to the shellcode via SetThreadContext (fires KERNEL_THREATINT_TASK_SETTHREADCONTEXT cross-process), then ResumeThread. The shellcode atomically increments a counter (shared across attacker and victim via the section's shared physical pages) and infinite-loops. Attacker verifies via LOCAL read of its own view (physically shared, no cross-process read needed) then terminates the victim. This is a REAL documented advanced malware technique (Doppelgänging-family without transactions, or 'Herpaderping'-adjacent) and exercises BOTH the new section-mapping detection rule AND the pre-existing thread-hijack rule — demonstrating cascade ordering correctly picks the more-specific section-mapping label.

extra.expected_fingerprint: 1x MAPVIEW_REMOTE (attacker maps shared section into victim's address space — THE key cross-process event of section-based delivery), 1x SETTHREADCONTEXT_REMOTE (RIP redirect to shellcode entry), 1x CreateProcess (KernelProcess provider — victim is a fresh process launched by the attacker in CREATE_SUSPENDED). Notably absent: 0x ALLOCVM_REMOTE (no VirtualAllocEx — shared section delivery replaces it), 0x WRITEVM_REMOTE (no WriteProcessMemory — shared physical pages replace it), 0x THREAD_CREATE_REMOTE (no CreateRemoteThread — victim's own main thread runs the payload). Expected classifier verdict: injection.section_mapping via section_mapping.ti_mapview rule (fires at cascade position 1). This tests: (a) that the new MAPVIEW detector fires on real data, (b) that the section_mapping rule wins the cascade over the also-matching thread_hijack rule, (c) that the classifier correctly labels the DELIVERY primitive (section mapping) rather than the TRIGGER primitive (thread hijack).
